ruff.scope: changed Python sources, scripts and tests

fixed: Zero-rate assignments were not rejected by independent validation.
Output path subsets could redefine reconstructed task demand; now recomputed from the complete input domain.
Python/native scalar and period validation differed.
Long task-rate correction sums needed per-product/per-addition outward rounding on binary64 long double.
Windows CMake, versioned CPLEX libraries, hashing, UTC and executable suffix support.
Joint-cut top-8 selection stored and sorted all eligible task pairs.
Optional Gurobi dependency and current versus historical experiment entrypoints.
Positive solver budget required by the new runner.
review.correction_of_initial_review_claim: MSVC std::filesystem::rename already replaces regular target files. Explicit Win32 replacement is platform implementation/test coverage, not a confirmed prior second-write bug.
cross_reviews: Independent review of complete-domain streaming validation found no confirmed defect.
Runner state, fingerprints and overwrite protection reviewed independently.
Server probe targets and runbook/CMake/script consistency reviewed independently.

limitations: Only macOS execution verified in this session; Windows installation, compiler, license and acceptance remain a separate gate.
Small fixtures establish local contracts, not production performance or a general formal numerical proof.
Physical reconstruction needs a complete input-domain scan and can be expensive. The server runner limits validator process wall time; direct build_operations calls have no internal scan budget.
General-L joint candidate enumeration remains O(Q^2); only candidate storage and sorting were reduced.
ALNS/support/index/feedback remain L2 K2; the portable runner disables all four elsewhere.
Historical Python optimization and dated POSIX batch tools remain for their original semantics and are not current Windows production entrypoints.
Saved-output-dependent report tests were excluded to avoid reading old experiment outputs.
